strings.name: Christian Sewing
strings.role: Deutsche Bank CEO and Chairman of the Management Board
strings.summary: Christian Sewing is a German banker who joined Deutsche Bank in 1989 and became CEO in 2018 after roles in credit, risk and audit. He led business restructuring; assessments of his tenure must also consider workforce reductions, compliance issues and remediation responsibilities.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026, including the bank's response to media reports that day. Management and Supervisory Boards, corporate statements and independent findings, and reported results and future targets are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Deutsche Bank's restructuring, resizing investment banking and strengthening corporate and retail finance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Professional education
strings.facts.f1.value: He completed bank apprenticeship training and later earned a diploma from Bankakademie Bielefeld and Hamburg; this is not recast as an unverified university degree or MBA.
strings.facts.f2.label: Governance structure
strings.facts.f2.value: The CEO and Management Board chairman belongs to executive management, not the chairmanship of the Supervisory Board; the Supervisory Board appoints the CEO.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Restructuring and employment
strings.highlights.h1.text: The 2019 plan scaled back equities sales and trading and created a Corporate Bank division, while targeting a reduction of about 18,000 full-time-equivalent positions by 2022; a plan is not evidence that cuts were already completed.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Limits of compliance assessments
strings.highlights.h2.text: In November 2026 the bank responded to investigative reporting by emphasizing historical issues and investment in controls. Its position is not independent exoneration, nor does reporting itself constitute a judicial finding of personal wrongdoing by Sewing.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Bank responds to investigative reporting
strings.timeline.t1.text: Deutsche Bank said the matters dated back years, that controls had been strengthened and that outstanding remediation would continue; these are the bank's own statements.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Third-quarter results released
strings.timeline.t2.text: The bank reported net revenues of €8.3 billion, pre-tax profit of €2.6 billion and post-tax profit of €1.9 billion, quoting current CEO Sewing.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Mandate extended to 2029
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Supervisory Board extended his contract by three years to April 2029; this does not mean the future term has already been served.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Major restructuring announced
strings.timeline.t4.text: A Corporate Bank division was established, with an exit from equities sales and trading while retaining targeted equity capital markets activities.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Chief Executive Officer
strings.timeline.t5.text: The appointment took immediate effect, replacing John Cryan; Cryan left the bank at month-end, which was not the CEO handover date.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins the Management Board
strings.timeline.t6.text: He assumed group-level management duties and subsequently responsibility for Private & Commercial Banking.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leads Group Audit
strings.timeline.t7.text: He became head of Group Audit after working in credit and risk management.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Deutsche Bank
strings.timeline.t8.text: He began his career path at the bank and later worked in several international financial centers.
